messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: Dedicated pool 'eu-west-1-dedicated-2' p99 latency breach detected, > 10s for streaming responses. Auto-escalation threshold exceeded, paging on-call.
Michelle (SRE): I'm on it. seeing sustained queue depth rising on that pool, queue.depth ~ 480 (capacity 512) and warmup failures spiking.
Raj (Runtime): Confirming, kernel warmup latencies for 8-bit quantized model v2-q8 are ~2.2s per slot which is stalling streaming handshakes. p95 = 1.9s, p99 = 10.7s.
Oleg (Eng Runtime): Logs show a pattern of cold-slot preemption during autoscale: warmup tasks getting preempted by lower-priority burst allocations. grabbing stack traces now.
Ashley (PM): Customer impact: 3 enterprise tenants flagged with degraded streaming (EU region). Connor from CS is pulling customer logs.
Connor (CS): Notified customers in thread, one reported partial responses and reconnects. They're on a critical demo today.
Nina (Support): Adding customer ticket IDs: #INC-3421, #INC-3423, customers asked for ETA.
Michelle (SRE): Short-term mitigation: disabling autoscale preemption for this pool and forcing allocation of warmup-capable slots. Executing now: `./infractl pool update eu-west-1-dedicated-2 --no-preempt`.
oncall-bot: Command accepted, change submitted by michelle-sre, run id 6f3a2b.
Raj (Runtime): Also enabling immediate fallback routing for affected app routes to model variant v2-cpu-fallback to preserve streaming continuity. Patch: `routing.set-fallback --route prod/* --model v2-cpu-fallback`.
Oleg (Eng Runtime): Pushing a hotfix to warmup orchestrator to mark warmup tasks non-preemptible for 5 minutes: `git rev: hotfix/warmup-lock` and deploying.
Michelle (SRE): After toggle, queue depth dropped from 480 -> 210 over 3 mins. p95 trending down to 750ms, p99 ~ 2.5s. Still watching tail.
Raj (Runtime): Root cause hypothesis: new scheduling policy combined with recent quantized kernel update created longer warmup than autoscaler tolerates, causing churn and slot thrashing under burst.
Ashley (PM): @Connor please let customers know we've applied mitigations and are monitoring. Offer to route their traffic to hosted hosted-fallback region temporarily.
Connor (CS): Notified customers. One accepted hosted-fallback, routing change in progress.
Nina (Support): Customers appreciate the update, asking for postmortem and ETA for full fix.
Michelle (SRE): Medium-term: will increase warmup concurrency for this pool and adjust autoscaler warmup window from 30s -> 90s for quantized models. Filing follow-up RFC.
Raj (Runtime): Also rolling back the quantized kernel tweak on eu-west pool and re-rolling with a guarded rollout. Rollback command: `release rollback kernel-q8 2026-03-14-ct1`.
Oleg (Eng Runtime): Gathering traces showing KV cache cold miss rate spike from 4% -> 42% during the incident; caching policy will be tuned.
oncall-bot: Incident severity upgraded to Sev2 at 1759008800 due to customer-impacting demo interruptions.
Michelle (SRE): Handoff timeline: I'll be primary until +2h then hand to night oncall. Leaving runbook notes: `incident:1759008642/notes` contains mitigation steps.
Raj (Runtime): Telemetry: p95 streaming latency baseline pre-incident 220ms, during incident peaked 2.1s, p99 peaked 11.3s. Token throughput dropped ~18% due to stalled streams.
Oleg (Eng Runtime): Deploys completed, warmup lock active. Observing streaming stalls clear on nodes that finished warmup. Some legacy slots still cold; manual warmup script applied: `infractl node warmup --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-2 --nodes 5`.
Michelle (SRE): Can we add a short-term safety: cap incoming burst concurrency at 85% of pool capacity to avoid handshake storms? Proposing `rate-limit --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-2 --burst 85%`.
Raj (Runtime): Applied cap. Immediate reduction in new cold handshakes. p99 now 1.2s and trending down.
Ashley (PM): Good mitigation. Please keep me posted on ETA for full rollback/patch and a customer-facing timeline.
Connor (CS): Customers updated, one asks for a brief postmortem email when available.
Nina (Support): I'll draft the customer note and share with PM for approval.
Michelle (SRE): Summary of actions: 1) Disabled preemption, 2) Enabled fallback routing, 3) Deployed warmup-lock hotfix, 4) Manual node warmups, 5) Applied burst cap, 6) Rolling kernel rollback.
Raj (Runtime): Next steps: revert kernel change cluster-wide only after a canary with extended warmup window completes. Suggested canary size: 5% traffic for 1h.
Oleg (Eng Runtime): Collecting artifacts: warmup traces, scheduler decisions, KV miss logs, and warmup task preemption traces. Uploading to /artifacts/incidents/1759008642.tar.gz
Michelle (SRE): Lowering page severity to monitoring at 1759013200 — p99 under 1s and queue < 120. Handoff to night: @oncall-night please monitor the rollout and customer escalations.
oncall-bot: Handoff acknowledged: oncall-night is now primary. Escalation channel created: #incident-1759008642-handoff.
Ashley (PM): Thanks team. Please include a timeline and follow-up postmortem with remediation (autoscaler warmup tuning + scheduler non-preemptive policy for warmup). I'll schedule a post-incident review tomorrow.
Connor (CS): Will coordinate customer follow-ups after postmortem draft.
Michelle (SRE): Closing note: if any regression occurs revert `--no-preempt` and re-enable routing toggles. Leaving runbook pointer and contact list in the handoff channel.
oncall-bot: Incident closed for paging at 1759015400. Monitoring continues.
